Torpid

/TOR-pid/ - the stress falls on TOR · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Torpid means lethargic, dormant, lacking motion.

The novel's detective spends a torpid month between cases, barely leaving the armchair until the telegram arrives.

Worked Example

The barn's resident bats go torpid in the cold months, folded like closed umbrellas under the ridge beam, deaf to the tractor coughing to life below them.

Torpid is deeper than slow: it's the near-shutdown of a system idling at its minimum—an animal in winter, a market with no buyers, a mind before coffee. Languid drifts; torpid has all but stopped.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

sluggish: moving, but slowly and with effort

numb: deadened to sensation, often from cold

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

active: up and doing

brisk: quick, energetic, and efficient

Where it sits · how much motion is still left — sluggish → torpid → lifeless

sluggish vs. torpid: Sluggish is the milder slowdown—a sluggish engine still turns over, grumbling but running.

lifeless vs. torpid: Lifeless goes further than sluggish—it means no motion left at all, while torpid keeps a faint pulse idling under the stillness.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — torp

Root — torp: to be numb, stiff (Latin torpere)

Suffix — -id

Suffix — -id: in a state of

Put it together

Put it together: Torp- (to be numb or stiff, from Latin torpere) + -id (in a state of) = in a numbed state. The same suffix builds this unit's languid and placid; torpid is the coldest of the three—function dialed down to a flicker.

Use the root in a new word: torpor

Use the root in a new word: torpor: Swap the suffix and the state becomes a noun: the museum's afternoon torpor broke only when the fire alarm tripped.

Word Choice

formal / scientific tinge

Torpid is the shutdown word—biologists use it for hibernating animals, and it fits anything idling at its minimum: markets, committees, inboxes. Its unit-mates grade the dimmer switch: languid is weak but still flowing, somnolent is specifically sleepy, torpid has nearly stopped. If the thing is permanently dead rather than dormant, torpid is too gentle.
